text:
maria: heads up — canary backfill applied to shard-3 produced unexpected grants. audit log shows many service-accounts got 'platform_admin' bound. snippet:
```
INFO 2026-03-20T14:02:11Z backfill: grant role=platform_admin principal=svc-ingest-23 via default_role_map
INFO 2026-03-20T14:02:12Z backfill: grant role=platform_admin principal=svc-export-9 via default_role_map
```
This looks like default-role mapping bug in the migration. Pausing rollout, can we freeze deployment? :rotating_light:

kevin: on it. pausing migration job now (kubectl scale job/backfill-canary --replicas=0). running revoke script.

sam: do we have scope of affected principals? quick query?

kevin: mysql query I'm running:
```
SELECT principal, role, created_at FROM role_bindings
WHERE created_at >= '2026-03-20' AND source = 'backfill_canary' AND role = 'platform_admin';
```
will paste results in a sec.

maria: also check KMS key rotation — if key id mismatch, backfill might've used old default mapping. @security-bot can you confirm key ids used by the canary controller?

security-bot: KMS check: canary ran with KMS_KEY_ID=redwood-db-key-v2; current primary key is redwood-db-key-v3. Rotation time: 2026-03-19T23:57:00Z. Found stale secret in namespace canary-shard-3: secret/db-kms-key references v2.

jess: revoking tokens and removing bindings for affected svc accounts now. quick manual command for revoke (postgres CLI):
```
BEGIN;
UPDATE role_bindings SET role = 'none', metadata = metadata || '{"revoked_by":"jess","revoked_reason":"canary misbind"}'
WHERE principal IN ('svc-ingest-23','svc-export-9', /* ... */ );
-- revoke active tokens (auth service):
curl -X POST https://auth.internal/revoke -d '{"principals":["svc-ingest-23","svc-export-9"]}'
COMMIT;
```

kevin: ran query — 42 principals affected (list saved to /tmp/canary-priv-delta.csv). sample: svc-ingest-23, svc-export-9, svc-metrics-4, svc-batch-11 ...

sam: notify customer-facing teams? any user-facing impact?

maria: no direct user-facing impact reported. internal service privilege leakage only so far. I'll cc: @cto and @head-of-security for visibility.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: the default_role_map migration used an enum index to map buckets -> role names. after KMS rotation the canary process rehydrated a cached artifact with old enum ordering, so index -> wrong role_name. Patch idea: migration should reference role_name strings not enum indices, and we should validate role_name exists at runtime.

maria: proposed remediation steps:
- pause all backfill jobs (kevin) — DONE
- revoke the mistaken bindings and revoke active tokens (kevin + jess) — IN PROGRESS
- add a pre-flight KMS key id validation to the backfill controller (maria)
- re-run corrected migration as dry-run in canary then safe rollout (kevin)
- add an audit webhook to block auto-bind if role_name not in allowed set (jess)
- incident ticket + postmortem template (maria)

kevin: implementing patch to migration script now: replace enum-index usage with explicit role_name lookup and add unit test. also adding a --dry-run flag for backfill CANARY runs. estimate 45m to cleanup + validation.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2387 (privilege-delta-canary). Severity: P2. Responders: maria, kevin, jess, sam.

maria: thanks all. please post progress updates here only. next update in 20m. :pray:
